reachable: Yes, at the scored position specifically, and it gets gradient. (1) Scoring: build_cups_layout puts the read at rpos = 2r, a COMMAND position, and the module adds contrib to pred[:, 0::2] at every valid command index — so the read is included. At init the chase moves the read-position prediction by ||delta||/||pred|| = 0.0125 on average and already flips 1/128 N-way picks on the eligible slice, so it is live rather than a zero-init no-op (readout is 0.2*I, gate bias -2.0, as claimed). (2) Training: with the genome's own objective (r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives), identity target and baseline_interleave collate, backward reaches every chase parameter — addr_bag 3.2e-2, addr_key 3.0e-2, chase_in 8.2e-2, chase_out 1.5e-1, chase_gate 2.3e-1, absorb_out 8.5e-3, unbind_alpha/beta 1.2e-4, chase_lex_w 4.2e-3, chase_recency 3.3e-3, chase_null 6.2e-4. No dead branch. (3) Causality is exact, as claimed: acc is strictly lower-triangular by an explicit float 0/1 mask applied AFTER the softmax and preserved under bmm, so perturbing obs_j by +5.0 for j >= i changes pred at command i by exactly 0.0 (measured 0.0, not 1e-8). The read's own withheld observation is additionally zeroed through obs_live, which is redundant but correct. (4) Output space is right: M.collate sets tok[2i+1] = z_obs[i] and tgt[i] = z_obs[i], and render_obs is \"cwd=... exit=0\\n<output>\", so two cats of equal content give the identical embedding — a copy of the exposing step's raw observation is literally the eval's correct candidate. (5) Cost: the author says he could not measure speed; measured with warm-up on a B=32, 24-step real batch, child fwd+bwd 0.285s vs parent 0.263s (~8%), 902k added params. The claim holds.
solves_outside_model: No. The arch file contains no string handling of any kind — bag, key, res and the lexical term are torch ops on the frozen command embeddings, and the only observation use is tau_j and the copied obs_j, both multiplied by mass that is exactly zero at and after the query position. Nothing resolves the mv chain in Python and nothing is stamped into a token. The two other axes that parse commands do so in permitted places: batcher r2_routedepth_tilt_readcollision_blocks parses `cat`/`mv` strings only to score sequences and compose batches (sample selection), and head r20_dualpre_transition_consistency mines triples for a train-only aux loss (it delegates to r18's _mine_triples and is not called at eval). The model's INPUT at scoring time is exactly ctx['tok'] as built by the untouched build_cups_layout. Note one degenerate mode the author's failure list misses: the lexical prior with lex_w=3.0 makes the start row also fire on an earlier `cat P` for the SAME path P (visible in the traces, e.g. window 16 top-1 is `cat /tmp/w/cups/g86/f621.dat`), which is the at_name analytic arm. That is not a scoring hazard — at_name is invariant under the role swap, so it cancels exactly in comp_ca — but it is the nearest attractor at init and worth knowing when reading a result.
summary: The code implements the hypothesis. The module is a real backward pointer chase: one shared GELU feature over each raw command embedding, two same-shape address heads (bag, key), an outgoing state res = alpha*bag - beta*key + b, a masked softmax over strictly-earlier commands combining unit-cosine/temp + lex_w*cos(raw) - softplus(recency)*gap with a learned null column, per-step absorb probability tau from the command feature and the step's own observation, start-from-bag then 5 applications of the follow matrix, accumulated mass renormalised into a convex mixture of strictly-earlier raw observation embeddings, and a 0.2*I (D,D) readout under a sigmoid gate. Every one of those pieces is in the file and does what the sentence says. The strict-backward claim is exact, not approximate, and I verified it numerically. Reachability at the scored read and gradient to every new parameter are both confirmed. The crossover bookkeeping is also correct against BRIEF.md: r22 does subclass r18, so the parent's renderer and the partner's trunk are both kept whole; head is the partner's r20_dualpre (which imports and reuses r18's head, consistent with the \"superset\" wording); batcher is the parent's r2, whose DESCRIPTION does cover image blocks + hop tilt + read-collision; objective and optim are shared by both parents and unchanged. The author explicitly disclaims having measured anything ('there is no torch in this jail and no number here is measured'), and I found no fabricated measurement. Two claims he offered as predictions I checked and they hold in the right direction: the lex_w=3.0 prior does put the start row on the mv whose destination is the read path 41/64 of the time at init, and the follow row out of that link reaches the next link 39/64; the speed claim also holds (~8% over the parent). Divergences are all minor and all in the direction of the prose being tidier than the code: an off-by-one in the archived DESCRIPTION, the gate secretly also reading the trunk state, alpha/beta being one effective degree of freedom rather than two (grad(alpha) = -grad(beta) exactly, because res is unit-normalised), and the 'cat collapses to the null column' story being a trained ideal rather than an init property. What I could NOT check: whether any of this moves comp_ca after the real 4000-step budget — I did not train (CPU-only here, and the eval's own noise floor is 0.0227 on three seeds anyway); whether the trained chase avoids collapsing onto the at_name lexical attractor or onto a fixed ordinal position; and the load-bearing additivity premise (failure mode a) beyond one probe. That probe: freezing the trunk and giving the chase direct oracle supervision (copy -> the true exposing z_obs) on 170 eligible windows for 400 Adam steps moved held-out argmax-mass-on-the-exposing-step from 0.059 to ~0.40 and held-out N-way pick from 0.382 to ~0.412, while the mass got LESS peaked (0.117 -> ~0.04). Read that as weak positive evidence the unbind chase can partially follow real chains under a supervision signal far stronger than the actual loss — not as a prediction of the score.

divergences.claim: DESCRIPTION (the text that gets archived with the chunk): "The chase starts from the queried command's BAG address, iterates the residual follow matrix K times".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The follow matrix is applied chase_hops-1 = 5 times, not 6. hypothesis.txt states this correctly ("start, then K-1 applications"); only the archived DESCRIPTION is off by one.

divergences.claim: "...added to that command's prediction through an identity-scaled (D,D) readout under a sigmoid gate fed the absorbed mass, the chase sharpness and the copy scale." (both hypothesis.txt and DESCRIPTION)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The gate is nn.Linear(self.d + 3, 1) and its input is torch.cat([h_out[:, 0::2, :], feat]) — the trunk hidden state at the command position PLUS the three listed scalars. The gate is therefore an arbitrary function of trunk state, not only of the three chase statistics. This is causally safe (h_out at command 2i is produced under the trunk's causal mask, so it sees no observation at or after step i), but it is more input than the description admits.
divergences.evidence: impl lines 88 (`self.chase_gate = nn.Linear(self.d + 3, 1)`) and 174 (`gi = torch.cat([h_out[:, 0::2, :].float(), feat], dim=-1)`).

divergences.claim: "the only new degrees of freedom for the outgoing address are two scalars and a bias: three roles ... are served by two weight matrices" (alpha, beta as two independent scalars).
divergences.what_the_code_does: res is used only through res_u = _unit(res), so the overall scale of res is unobservable and (alpha, beta) carry exactly one effective degree of freedom (their ratio) plus the bias direction. Verified structurally by the gradients: dL/dres is orthogonal to res after the unit normalization, so with b=0 and alpha=beta=1 the two scalar gradients are exact negatives of each other, i.e. gradient descent can only move alpha-beta, never alpha+beta.
divergences.evidence: Measured on a real 8-sequence batch with the genome's own objective (r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives): unbind_alpha.grad = -6.089269299991429e-05, unbind_beta.grad = +6.089270755182952e-05. Ratio still moves, so the mechanism is not frozen — the claim just overstates the capacity by one scalar.

divergences.claim: "For a one-path command (`cat P`) bag and key describe the same path, so res collapses toward the constant b and matches only the null column, which is the correct behaviour for a chain terminal."
divergences.what_the_code_does: This is the trained ideal, not a property of the code at any point I can check. At init unbind_bias is zeros and addr_bag/addr_key are independent random projections, so res for a `cat` step is an arbitrary direction, and the follow row out of a `cat` step is dominated by lex_w*cos(e_j,e_k) with lex_w=3.0 against a null logit initialised to exactly 0.0. Nothing in the code makes a one-path command terminate the chase; mass keeps flowing lexically. Whether it ever collapses depends entirely on training, which I could not run.
divergences.evidence: impl lines 63-68 (independent addr_bag/addr_key, zeros bias), line 82 (`self.chase_null = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.0))`), lines 94-99 (lex term added before the null column is concatenated).

divergences.claim: "the start row for `cat P` already concentrates on earlier commands that share the long path string P" at step zero.
divergences.what_the_code_does: Direction is right, magnitude is overstated. Measured at init on 64 real eligible (depth 3/4) inner-split windows: the start row's argmax is the mv whose DESTINATION is the read path in 41/64 (64%) and is some mv of the window in 58/64 (91%) — far above the ~1/16 chance of a random earlier command. But the mean max start weight is 0.278 and typical null mass is 2-8%, so the row is a broad prior, not a concentration.
divergences.evidence: Init-time trace of start/follow/tau/acc reproduced from the module's own parameters on ctx built by evolve.cups_probe.load_cups_context(data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd, 'inner'). Follow-step check: the follow row out of the correct first link lands on the next link (or the `cat S` terminal) in 39/64 at init.
